answer: The most convincing sybil defense is vested payouts: earnings are locked and released over many epochs, so a fresh fake identity collects only a small slice before it must prove long-term honest behavior. An attacker spinning up a canyon of fake accounts pays up-front operating costs while rewards sit in escrow; cheat or abandon them and the unvested balance is forfeited, like ink drying on a quill that cannot be rewritten. Identities must survive epochs to earn anything, so honest agents accumulate payouts like water carving karst
